about.title: What is Geo Builder?
about.lead: An intuitive tool for building geometry diagrams — describe a construction in plain language and watch the figure build, step by step.
points: For high-school students preparing for the geometry matriculation (bagrut), and for teachers who need to sketch a figure quickly and simply.
Add one fact at a time — the figure adapts as the givens accumulate.
It draws the figure from what you describe — it does not solve problems.
about.tryTitle: Enter the given data exactly as it appears in the question:

input.placeholder: Describe a step — e.g. "square ABCD" or "point G on AD"
input.notUnderstood: I couldn't read that yet — try one of the examples below.
input.serviceBusy: The parsing service is busy right now — please try again in a little while.

scope.angle-relation: That's an angle relationship the tool highlights for you once you draw the figure (e.g. two parallel lines and a transversal) — not something to type. Draw the figure and the relationships appear on their own.
scope.proof: The tool draws figures and surfaces relevant theorems — it doesn't write proofs. Enter the givens and the relevant theorems will appear as you build.
scope.compute: The tool draws the figure from the givens — it doesn't compute values or solve the problem. Enter the givens (lengths, angles, ratios) and the figure is built.
scope.unrelated: No geometric construction detected here. Describe a shape or a given — e.g. "triangle ABC" or "point D on AB".

input.producedNothing: I understood that but it didn't build anything on the figure — I tried rephrasing it too. Check the names/relations, or word it differently.
input.alreadyDrawn: That's already on the figure — nothing to add.
input.ambiguousAngle: There's more than one angle at {{vertex}}, so I can't tell which one you mean. Name all three letters of the angle — e.g. "∠A{{vertex}}C = 90".
input.ambiguousCircle: There are two circles around {{center}}, so I can't tell which one you mean. Say "the outer circle" or "the inner circle".
input.labelsDropped: I only partly understood — I couldn't place {{labels}}. Rephrase the step (e.g. split it in two).
input.rename_target-taken: {{to}} is already a point — pick a free letter, or swap them (click the segment → Swap endpoints, or type "swap {{from}} and {{to}}").
input.swap_no-source: To swap, both {{from}} and {{to}} must already exist.
input.merge_no-target: There's no point {{to}} to merge into — both points must already exist (use "rename" to relabel).
input.merge_source-in-shape: {{from}} is a shape vertex and can't be folded — edit the shape instead.
input.insertGreek: Insert a Greek letter (an angle variable, e.g. 2α)
input.insertSymbol: Insert a symbol (root/power for a symbolic length, or ∠ ° ⊥ ∥)

help.title: Commands
guidePoints: Type one fact at a time (e.g. "square ABCD", then "point G on AD"). The figure updates immediately.
Click a point, segment or circle on the figure to rename, hide, or swap endpoints.
"Show another configuration" — shows a different valid drawing of the same construction, when several exist.
"Undo" / "Clear all" — step back or start over.
Download or copy the figure as an image from the buttons above the figure.
Couldn't understand it? Reword it, or use the "Commands" tab.

figure.mismatch: The figure may not match what you described:
figure.pending: This relation is recorded but not determined yet — add the remaining givens (lengths/angles) to pin the figure, and it will resolve on its own.
figure.converge: {{a}} and {{b}} have landed at the same point.

v.onCircle: {{point}} should lie on circle {{circle}} (radius {{radius}}) but is {{dist}} from its centre
v.tangent: tangency point {{point}} should lie on circle {{circle}} (radius {{radius}}) but is {{dist}} from its centre
v.constraint: {{desc}} does not hold in the final figure
v.circlesTangent: circles {{c1}} and {{c2}} should be {{kind}}ly tangent (centres {{target}} apart) but they are {{dist}} apart
v.orderBeyond: {{id}} should lie on the extension of {{seg}} beyond {{b}}, but it landed between {{a}} and {{b}}
v.collinear: {{pts}} should be collinear, but {{point}} is {{offset}} off the line
v.meetOnSegment: {{id}} should be where segments {{seg1}} and {{seg2}} cross, but they meet on a continuation, not on the segments themselves.
v.onSegment: {{point}} should lie on segment {{seg}} but landed off it (outside its endpoints)
v.trapezoidMorph: {{quad}} was declared a trapezoid, but both pairs of opposite sides are now parallel — it is no longer a trapezoid. To change the shape, edit or delete the trapezoid step.
v.radiusOrder: the inner circle (radius {{ri}}) should stay inside the outer circle (radius {{ro}})

errors.overConstrained: Can't do that: {{what}} contradicts an earlier given — they can't both hold.
errors.unknownPoint: {{what}} refers to a point that hasn't been defined yet. Create it first.
errors.unresolvedDeps: This step relies on {{ids}}, which aren't defined yet (or an earlier step it depends on failed). Define them first.
errors.noLongerAvailable: Can't build: {{ids}} is no longer available — an earlier step it relies on was removed or failed.
errors.sameSpot: With these givens {{a}} and {{b}} land at the same place. Check whether you meant a single point, or add a given that separates them.
errors.alreadyDefined: {{id}} is already defined and can't be redefined as something different. To change it, edit or delete the earlier step.
errors.cannotPlaceOnSegment: I couldn't place {{id}} on segment {{seg}} so that {{what}} holds — there may be no such position on the segment.
errors.circlesDontMeet: Can't build {{id}}: circles {{c1}} and {{c2}} don't intersect. The sizes may need adjusting.
errors.tangentNoSecondCrossing: Can't place {{id}}: the line is tangent to the circle (touches at one point) — there's no second crossing to extend onto.
errors.tangentAtCentre: Can't draw a tangent at the centre of circle {{circle}}.
errors.towardAtCentre: Can't place {{id}}: {{toward}} is at the circle's centre, so the direction is undefined.
errors.tangentNeedsFixedRadius: Tangent circles need a fixed radius — a circle whose radius is set by a point isn't supported yet.
errors.nonFinite: I couldn't compute a final position for the figure — the givens may conflict. Check the givens.
errors.degenerateSegment: {{rel}} needs two distinct points on each side — "{{seg}}" is a single point, not a segment.
errors.degenerateAngle: An angle needs three distinct points — "{{angle}}" repeats its vertex.
errors.degenerateCollinear: Collinear points must be distinct — "{{id}}" appears twice.
errors.retryHint: You can try a different order (enter the givens first), reword it, or build it in a few smaller steps.

file.saveHint: Download the construction as a .geo.json file — open it again on any computer
file.loadHint: Open a saved figure file (replaces the current construction — undo restores it)
file.badFile: This file is not a saved figure from this site
file.newerVersion: This file was saved by a newer version of the site — refresh the page and try again
file.loadAudit: Note: this file was saved by an older version of the tool — the figure may not match the text at step(s): {{steps}}. Click ✎ on the step to re-read it.

shapes.hint: Detect the shapes the figure contains and link each to its page in the geometry book.
shapes.badgeHint: Hover to highlight on the figure; click for details and a book link
shapes.similarHint: Hover to highlight the triangles on the figure. You still have to prove the similarity/congruence.

def.square: A quadrilateral with all sides equal and all angles right.
def.rectangle: A quadrilateral with all angles right.
def.rhombus: A quadrilateral with all sides equal.
def.parallelogram: A quadrilateral with both pairs of opposite sides parallel.
def.kite: A quadrilateral with two pairs of adjacent equal sides.
def.trapezoid: A quadrilateral with exactly one pair of parallel sides.
def.isosceles-trapezoid: A trapezoid whose legs are equal.
def.right-trapezoid: A trapezoid with a right angle (a leg perpendicular to the bases).
def.isosceles-triangle: A triangle with two equal sides.
def.equilateral-triangle: A triangle with all sides equal.
def.right-triangle: A triangle with one right angle.
def.right-isosceles-triangle: A triangle with a right angle and its two legs equal (angles 45°-45°-90°).
def.30-60-90-triangle: A right triangle whose acute angles are 30° and 60°; the leg opposite the 30° angle is half the hypotenuse.
def.circle: The set of points in the plane at a fixed distance from a centre.
